items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.summary: The transformer paper: a way to train on language in parallel across many chips, which nearly every large model since is built on.

items.title: AlphaZero learns chess from the rules
items.summary: Given only the rules, a program taught itself chess and shogi by playing itself and beat the best engine of the day.

items.title: GPT-1: pretrain then fine-tune
items.summary: The paper that showed training a model on raw text first, then tuning it for a task, beats task-specific models; it is dated 11 June 2018.

items.title: BERT reads both directions
items.summary: Google's model weighed the words before and after a word at once, and set new records on eleven language tests.

items.title: GPT-2 held back, then released
items.summary: OpenAI put out a smaller version first, saying the full model could be misused to mass-produce fake text.

items.title: Scaling laws: bigger is predictable
items.summary: OpenAI published curves showing model quality rises smoothly with size, data and compute, which made spending predictable.

items.title: GPT-3: scale is the trick
items.summary: A 175-billion-parameter model that could take on new tasks from a prompt with no retraining.

items.title: AlphaFold 2 cracks protein folding
items.summary: Predicted protein shapes at near-experimental accuracy in a blind test, a 50-year-old problem.

items.title: DALL·E makes pictures from words
items.summary: Text-to-image generation that produced coherent images for short written prompts.

items.title: LaMDA built for conversation
items.summary: Google's conversational model, later at the centre of a public claim that it was sentient.

items.title: GitHub Copilot writes code
items.summary: A technical preview of autocomplete for programmers, built on OpenAI's models, the first mass coding assistant.

items.title: AlphaFold paper published in Nature
items.summary: The method behind the CASP14 result was published in full; DeepMind released structures for most known proteins in July 2022.

items.title: Chinchilla: models were under-trained
items.summary: DeepMind showed that, for a fixed compute budget, most large models were too big and fed too little text.

items.title: Stable Diffusion goes public
items.summary: Open weights for image generation, runnable on a home graphics card, and it spread in weeks.

items.title: ChatGPT opens to the public
items.summary: A chat interface on GPT-3.5 that reached a million users in days and made AI a consumer product.

items.title: Meta releases LLaMA weights
items.summary: A strong model released to researchers, which started the open-weight race.

items.title: Claude opens to the public
items.summary: Anthropic's first public model, offered as a chat assistant and an API.

items.title: GPT-4 released, reads images too
items.summary: OpenAI shipped a model that takes images as well as text and is far stronger on exams.

items.title: Llama 2 released with Microsoft
items.summary: Meta's next open model, launched with Microsoft as partner.

items.title: Mistral 7B: small and open
items.summary: A 7-billion-parameter model released with open weights, pitched as the most powerful of its size.

items.title: Gemini 1.0 launched as multimodal
items.summary: Google's first model family built for text, images and audio from the start, shipped in three sizes.

items.title: Sora shows a minute of video
items.summary: Text-to-video previews good enough to be mistaken for footage; not released to the public then.

items.title: Claude 3 family arrives
items.summary: Three models including a long-context version; Anthropic said the top one beat GPT-4 on some tests.

items.title: Llama 3 released
items.summary: Meta's next open model, in 8B and 70B sizes.

items.title: AlphaFold 3 predicts molecules
items.summary: Extended the model from proteins to DNA, RNA and small molecules, and how they interact.

items.title: GPT-4o talks in real time
items.summary: Voice conversation with near-instant replies, plus text and images, free to all users.

items.title: Llama 3.1 ships 405B open weights
items.summary: Meta's largest open model so far, released with a permissive licence.

items.title: o1 thinks before answering
items.summary: A model trained to work through long internal chains of reasoning before replying, much stronger on maths.

items.title: Nobel physics prize for neural networks
items.summary: Hopfield and Hinton shared the physics prize for work that made today's neural networks possible.

items.title: Nobel chemistry prize for protein work
items.summary: Baker, Hassabis and Jumper shared the chemistry prize, half of it for protein structure prediction.

items.title: o3 announced, not yet released
items.summary: OpenAI announced a new reasoning model, o3, three months after o1.

items.title: DeepSeek-R1: reasoning, open weights
items.summary: A Chinese lab published a reasoning model and its paper, with the weights released.

items.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and extended thinking
items.summary: Anthropic shipped a hybrid model that can think longer on demand, plus a coding tool.

items.title: Claude 4 models released
items.summary: Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, aimed at long-running coding agents.

items.title: Grok 4 released
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4, which it described as its most capable model.

items.title: Claude Opus 4.1 released
items.summary: An upgrade to Opus 4 focused on coding and agent work.

items.title: GPT-5 released
items.summary: OpenAI's unified model, pitched as expert-level at coding and reasoning, rolled into ChatGPT.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 4.5 released
items.summary: Anthropic's mid-size model, pitched as frontier intelligence at a lower price.

items.title: Gemini 3 launched
items.summary: Google's next flagship model, released to its app and to developers.

items.title: GPT-5.5 released
items.summary: OpenAI's model built around tools and long tasks, a step toward a "super app".

items.title: DeepSeek-V4, million-token context
items.summary: Open-weight models built for very long inputs, a million tokens, at a low price.

items.title: Claude Opus 5 launched
items.summary: Anthropic released Opus 5, which it pitched at coding and knowledge work.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash released
items.summary: A faster, cheaper DeepSeek model.

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 released
items.summary: Anthropic cut prices and pitched it at top-end coding performance.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon rolls out
items.summary: Google's frontier model for coding, enterprise work and cyber defence, to Pro and Ultra subscribers.

items.title: Nvidia's quarterly sales up 21%
items.summary: Revenue of $3.18bn for the quarter to 28 October, against $2.64bn a year earlier.

items.title: Microsoft puts $1bn into OpenAI
items.summary: First big-tech bet on the lab; Azure becomes its home.

items.title: Nvidia completes $7bn Mellanox purchase
items.summary: The networking deal, first announced in March 2019, closed.

items.title: Nvidia agrees $40bn deal for Arm
items.summary: Would have been the biggest chip deal ever; regulators later blocked it.

items.title: Nvidia's record quarter on AI demand
items.summary: Revenue of $6.51bn, up 68% on a year earlier; data-centre revenue $2.37bn, up 35%.

items.title: Nvidia and SoftBank drop the Arm deal
items.summary: Terminated over regulatory objections; Arm to pursue a public listing instead.

items.title: US blocks advanced chips to China
items.summary: New export controls on advanced computing chips and the equipment to make them.

items.title: Microsoft extends the OpenAI deal
items.summary: A multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment; Azure stays OpenAI's exclusive cloud.
items.label: Microsoft's OpenAI billions

items.title: Anthropic raises $450m Series C
items.summary: A funding round led by Spark Capital.

items.title: Nvidia's forecast sets off the AI rally
items.summary: Q1 revenue $7.19bn and a next-quarter outlook of $11.00bn.

items.title: Nvidia becomes a $1 trillion company
items.summary: First chipmaker to pass $1tn on AI demand.
items.label: Nvidia hits $1tn

items.title: Arm's shares begin trading after $51 IPO
items.summary: Priced at $51.00 per ADS in its IPO (the first sale of shares to the public); trading began on Nasdaq (a US stock market) under "ARM".

items.title: Amazon puts up to $4bn into Anthropic
items.summary: Investment tied to use of AWS as the lab's main cloud and chip supplier.

items.title: US tightens the chip export rules
items.summary: An update to the October 2022 controls, widening what is covered.

items.title: OpenAI board fires Sam Altman
items.summary: Board removes the CEO; staff threaten to leave; Microsoft offers to hire them.

items.title: Altman returns, new board seated
items.summary: Deal ends the crisis; Microsoft gets a non-voting board seat.

items.title: Nvidia passes $2 trillion
items.summary: Market value (what all its shares are worth) briefly reached $2tn, weeks after its results.
items.label: Nvidia hits $2tn

items.title: Nvidia's sales up 262% on the year
items.summary: Revenue of $26.0bn for the quarter to 28 April, up 262% from a year earlier.

items.title: Nvidia passes $3tn and tops Microsoft
items.summary: Worth $3.34tn at the close, the most valuable listed company in the world.

items.title: Sequoia's Cahn puts the AI gap at $600bn
items.summary: A Sequoia Capital partner wrote that the gap between AI revenue and the build-out had grown to a $600bn question.
items.label: First big bubble warning

items.title: OpenAI raises $6.6bn at $157bn
items.summary: A funding round valuing the lab at $157bn, the largest of the cycle to then.

items.title: Stargate: $500bn AI infrastructure venture
items.summary: OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and MGX announced $100bn to start and $500bn over four years.
items.label: Stargate: $500bn

items.title: DeepSeek rout: Nvidia loses $600bn
items.summary: Nvidia fell 17% in a day; the Guardian put the value lost at $600bn.
items.label: DeepSeek rout: $600bn

items.title: Anthropic raises at a $61.5bn valuation
items.summary: Series E funding round at a valuation (what investors say the whole company is worth) of $61.5bn.

items.title: CoreWeave IPO prices at $40
items.summary: 37.5m shares, $1.5bn raised, Nasdaq ticker "CRWV"; trading began 28 March.
items.label: CoreWeave lists

items.title: OpenAI raises $40bn at $300bn
items.summary: SoftBank-led round, the largest private financing ever at the time.

items.title: Nvidia takes a $4.5bn H20 charge
items.summary: A US licence requirement for H20 exports to China cost it $4.5bn of inventory in the quarter.

items.title: Meta pays $14.3bn for 49% of Scale AI
items.summary: Buys data-labelling capacity and brings in Alexandr Wang.

items.title: Nvidia becomes the first $4tn company
items.summary: The first listed company to reach a $4tn market value.

items.title: Apollo's Slok: AI more overvalued than in the 1990s
items.summary: Apollo's chief economist wrote that the top 10 S&P 500 companies (an index of 500 large US firms) are more overvalued now than they were in the 1990s IT bubble.
items.label: Slok: bigger than 1990s

items.title: Nvidia and AMD give US 15% of China sales
items.summary: An unusual arrangement to get export licences for H20 and MI308 chips.

items.title: Altman says investors are overexcited
items.summary: OpenAI's chief executive told reporters he thought investors as a whole were overexcited about AI, while still calling it vital.
items.label: Altman: yes, overexcited

items.title: Anthropic raises $13bn at $183bn
items.summary: Series F, the lab's largest round.

items.title: Oracle signs $300bn compute deal with OpenAI
items.summary: A five-year contract reported by the WSJ, with purchases starting in 2027.
items.label: Oracle's $300bn OpenAI deal

items.title: Nvidia to invest up to $100bn in OpenAI
items.summary: Letter of intent for at least 10GW of Nvidia systems; money released as capacity is deployed.
items.label: Nvidia's $100bn OpenAI bet

items.title: Stargate adds five more data-centre sites
items.summary: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank named five additional Stargate sites.

items.title: Bezos calls AI an industrial bubble
items.summary: At Italian Tech Week, Amazon's founder called the AI boom a kind of industrial bubble, not a financial one.
items.label: Bezos: industrial bubble

items.title: Microsoft takes 27% of OpenAI Group PBC
items.summary: Stake valued at about $135bn on an as-converted basis after the restructuring.

items.title: Nvidia first company to $5 trillion
items.summary: The first listed company to reach a $5tn market value.
items.label: Nvidia first to $5tn

items.title: Burry discloses shorts against Nvidia and Palantir
items.summary: "Big Short" investor bets against the AI trade and attacks chip depreciation accounting.
items.label: Burry bets against AI

items.title: Dalio: we are in bubble territory
items.summary: Bridgewater's founder said the picture was clear: the market was in bubble territory, though the bubble had not yet been pricked.
items.label: Dalio: in bubble territory

items.title: Nvidia memo answers the bubble charge
items.summary: Private memo to analysts names Burry and disputes his depreciation and circular-financing claims.

items.title: xAI raises $20bn Series E
items.summary: Upsized from $15bn, at about $230bn, with Nvidia, Cisco, Fidelity and Gulf funds.

items.title: SpaceX absorbs xAI in all-stock deal
items.summary: Combined entity implied near $1.25tn; the lab becomes part of Musk's rocket company.

items.title: Gurley expects an AI reset
items.summary: Benchmark's Bill Gurley told CNBC that waves create bubbles, and that an AI reset would come one day.
items.label: Gurley: an AI reset

items.title: OpenAI closes $122bn at $852bn
items.summary: Largest private round ever, more than double the October 2025 mark.
items.label: OpenAI at $852bn

items.title: Anthropic files confidentially for IPO
items.summary: First frontier lab to start a listing process; reported $965bn valuation after a $65bn round.

items.title: OpenAI 2025 accounts leak
items.summary: $13.07bn revenue against a $20.9bn operating loss; spending outran sales.

items.title: S&P cuts Oracle to BBB-
items.summary: Downgrade cites AI spending and concentration on OpenAI; one notch above junk.
items.label: Oracle cut to BBB-

items.title: Oracle credit insurance at 18-year high
items.summary: Cost of insuring Oracle debt against default hits a multi-year record; bonds sell off.

items.title: AI sell-off hits Korean chipmakers
items.summary: Seoul market at a three-month low as memory shares slide.

items.title: Asian chip shares plunge again
items.summary: Second day of AI selling in Asia; FTSE 100 nevertheless sets a record.

items.title: Oracle force majeure on Jupiter campus
items.summary: Notice on the $165bn OpenAI data-centre project; stock falls about 4%; project loan trades near 90 cents.

items.title: OpenAI revenue $20bn below plan
items.summary: September annualised revenue about $50bn, not the ~$70bn investors had been told.

items.title: IMF names AI correction a top risk
items.summary: Global Financial Stability Report lists AI, bond yields and cyber as triggers of turmoil.

items.title: Sell-off deepens on AI debt fears
items.summary: Tech shares fall again on US inflation and worry about how the buildout is financed.

items.title: Anthropic files public S-1
items.summary: Prospectus names Nasdaq, ticker "ANT"; first frontier lab to open its books.

items.title: Alphabet falls on weaker profits
items.summary: Q3 profit below expectations; more than $500bn of value wiped in a week.

items.title: 2026 hyperscaler capex tops $700bn
items.summary: TMT Finance puts 2026 capital spending by the big cloud companies above $700bn, up sharply on 2025.

items.title: OpenAI cuts round to $20bn at $1.25tn
items.summary: Reduced the target by $10bn; still seeking a $1.25tn post-money valuation.

items.title: $2.5tn+ wiped as AI stocks rout
items.summary: Nasdaq -5.5%, S&P 500 -4.4%, Dow down over 1,800 points; Democrats' midterm sweep blamed.
items.label: $2.5tn wiped in a day

items.title: OpenAI closes $11bn at $1.25tn
items.summary: First part of a round still expected to close in the coming weeks.

items.title: OpenAI Q3: $10bn revenue, $10.9bn loss
items.summary: Revenue up 50% on the quarter while operating losses matched it.

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns; Kress interim CEO
items.summary: Nvidia's founder leaves immediately; CFO Colette Kress takes over; Harvey Jones becomes first board chair.
items.label: Huang resigns
